title: scan_from 3-byte overlap in SSE frame detection — O(n) not O(n²)
description:
After appending bytes, scan_from = old_len.saturating_sub(3) rather than 0. This means frame delimiter scanning always starts 3 bytes before the new data, not at the beginning of buf. Without this, every new chunk causes a full re-scan of the entire accumulated buffer — O(n²) total work for a large frame. The 3-byte overlap is the minimum that covers all delimiter prefixes that could straddle a chunk boundary (

 at 4 bytes, 

 at 3, 

/ at 2). A future contributor who sees the walk-back-to-char-boundary loop might 'simplify' it to scan_from = 0, which would be functionally correct but O(n²). The comment is correct and essential — keep it.
